Enforcement Decree of the Act on Special Cases concerning the Payment of Retirement Compensation to Public Officials Disqualified from Appointment and Others

Article 1 (Purpose)
This Decree prescribes matters delegated by the Act on Special Cases concerning the Payment of Retirement Compensation to Public Officials Disqualified from Appointment and Others and matters necessary for its implementation. <Amended August 12, 2008>

Article 2 (Other Employees of the State or Local Governments)
“Other employees of the State or local governments prescribed by Presidential Decree” in the main clause of Article 2, subparagraph 1, of that Act (hereinafter the “Act”) means persons falling under any subparagraph of Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Pension Act who paid contributions under the Public Officials Pension Act. <Amended August 12, 2008>

Article 3 (Calculation of Retirement Compensation)
① Retirement benefits and retirement allowances or additional retirement benefits under Article 4(1) of the Act shall be calculated using the monthly remuneration under the Public Officials Pension Act or Military Pension Act at the end of the disqualified or automatically retired official's actual service. “Actual service period” shall be treated as the period of employment under the former Act and the period of military service under the latter Act. <Amended August 12, 2008>
② “Refund of contribution principal and interest” in Article 4(1) of the Act means contributions paid during actual service under the Public Officials Pension Act plus interest calculated by the Government Employees Pension Corporation with regard to the investment return of the Government Employees Pension Fund. For a person who ended actual service as a member of the military, it means contributions paid during actual service under the Military Pension Act plus interest calculated at the contribution refund rate under Article 4 of that Act and Article 5(1) of its Enforcement Decree. <Amended August 12, 2008; September 18, 2018>

Article 4 (Application for Payment)
① A person seeking payment under Article 4(2) of the Act shall submit the following documents by September 30, 2008 to the appointing authority or authority recommending appointment at the end of actual service. If that authority changed because of an institutional merger, abolition or similar reason, this means the successor authority; for a national official in the executive branch whose appointing or recommending authority is unclear, it means the Minister of Personnel Management. These meanings apply hereinafter. <Amended March 17, 2004; June 12, 2006; August 12, 2008; November 2, 2010; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014>
1. One application for payment in attached Form No. 1.
2. Deleted <June 12, 2006>.
3. One copy each of the person's family relations certificate and basic certificate. Where the person has died or been declared missing and these certificates do not establish the relevant facts, one certified copy of the removed family register or closed family relations certificate.
4. One designation of representative heir in Form No. 2, only where two or more heirs have equal priority.
5. One power of attorney to receive compensation in Form No. 3, only for an application through an agent because of emigration, hospitalization or another unavoidable reason.
6. One copy of other documents proving eligibility for compensation.
7. One copy of the applicant's bankbook for the account opened at the post office or financial institution where payment is desired.
② If the official has died, including a declaration of disappearance, and heirs apply under the proviso to Article 4(2) of the Act, two or more heirs of equal priority shall select a representative using Form No. 2 and apply through that representative.
③ If the official or heir cannot personally apply for or receive compensation because of emigration, hospitalization or another unavoidable reason, a power of attorney in Form No. 3 certified by one of the following shall be submitted:
1. Head of an overseas diplomatic mission, for emigration or other stay abroad.
2. Head of a medical institution, for hospitalization.
3. Head of the institution of confinement, for confinement in a prison or similar institution.
4. Head of the institution to which the person belonged when actual public service ended, in other cases.
④ The appointing or recommending authority receiving an application under paragraph ① shall verify the applicant's resident registration record through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent, the authority shall require the applicant to attach the record. <Amended November 2, 2010>

Article 5 (Investigation and Verification of Eligibility)
① The authority receiving the application shall investigate and verify whether the disqualified or automatically retired official is eligible for compensation under Article 4(1) of the Act (hereinafter an “eligible person”), with reference to:
1. The documents in the subparagraphs of Article 4(1).
2. The official's personnel record card or personnel and performance records.
3. Judgments and other court records.
4. Other documents needed to establish eligibility. <Amended August 12, 2008>
② If the investigation determines the person ineligible, the authority shall notify the applicant, stating reasons, within two months after receipt of the application. Where necessary for investigating and verifying eligibility, this period may be extended by up to one month.
③ If the person is determined eligible, the authority may request the President of the Government Employees Pension Corporation or the Minister of National Defense (only for persons who ended actual service as military personnel), using Form No. 4, to calculate the lump-sum retirement pension, lump-sum military retirement pension or lump-sum retirement benefit, and retirement allowance or additional retirement benefit for actual service. <Amended September 18, 2018>
④ The President or Minister receiving that request shall verify the calculation and notify the appointing or recommending authority within 30 days. <Amended September 18, 2018>
⑤ Upon receiving the calculation under paragraph ④, the authority shall prepare a retirement compensation payment statement in Form No. 5.

Article 6 (Payment and Receipt)
① The authority shall deliver a notice of decision in Form No. 6 to an applicant determined eligible under Article 5 within three months after receipt of the application. Where necessary to investigate and verify eligibility, this period may be extended by up to one month.
② Within six months after delivery of the notice, the authority shall deposit the compensation into the applicant's account at the post office or financial institution selected by the applicant. If payment within that period is difficult because of budgetary circumstances or similar reasons, it may be extended by up to six months, and the applicant shall be notified.
③ Compensation deposited under paragraph ② is deemed received by the applicant.

Article 7 (Benefit Claims under the Special Limitation Rule)
① An automatically retired official claiming benefits under Article 5(1) of the Act shall, by September 30, 2008, submit the benefit claim form prescribed by the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Pension Act, the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Accident Compensation Act or the Enforcement Decree of the Military Pension Act to the appointing or recommending authority at the end of actual service. <Amended August 12, 2008; September 18, 2018>
② The receiving authority shall investigate and verify the necessary matters and forward the claim to the President of the Government Employees Pension Corporation or the Minister of National Defense. <Amended September 18, 2018>
③ Submission to the appointing or recommending authority under paragraph ① is deemed submission to that President or Minister. <Amended September 18, 2018>

Article 8 Deleted <August 12, 2008>.
Article 9 Deleted <August 12, 2008>.

Article 10 (Certification of Actual Service)
A certificate of the disqualified or automatically retired official's actual service under Article 8 of the Act shall be issued in Form No. 7.

Article 11 (Recovery Interest and Costs)
① Interest added to compensation under the latter part of Article 9(1) of the Act shall be calculated from the day after payment to the date the appointing or recommending authority sends the recovery payment notice. If recovery is not paid by the deadline under Article 9(2) of the Act, overdue interest shall be calculated for the period of default. The rates and costs are:
1. Interest rate: for each year, the highest time-deposit rate applied by commercial banks nationwide as of January 1 of that year. If the recovery amount is not paid by the deadline, the overdue rate is the highest bank lending rate applied by those banks as of January 1 of each year during the overdue-interest calculation period.
2. Recovery costs: the amount calculated by the authority for investigation travel expenses and other expenses incurred in recovering compensation.
② Upon discovering grounds for recovery, the authority shall investigate without delay and send the recipient a recovery payment notice.

Article 12 (Temporary Task Force for Handling Appointment Disqualification)
① A temporary task force for handling appointment disqualification (hereinafter the “Task Force”) may be established and operated within the Ministry of Personnel Management to process and support efficiently the payment of compensation and related work for disqualified and automatically retired officials. <Amended August 12, 2008; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014>
② The Director-General for Personnel Policy of that Ministry shall head the Task Force. <Amended August 12, 2008; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014>
③ The Minister of Personnel Management may request administrative agencies and similar bodies to second their officials for the efficient operation of the Task Force. <Amended August 12, 2008; March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014>
